query: Which clinical factors best explain longer visit durations?

per_column.name: primary_complaint_type
per_column.rationale: The nature of the presenting complaint (chronic vs acute/emergency) plausibly drives both what treatment/workup occurs and how long the visit takes; a pre-encounter characteristic, so a genuine common cause rather than a mediator.

per_column.name: diagnostic_workup_required
per_column.rationale: Ordering extensive labs/imaging is on the causal path to longer duration and is itself a consequence of the clinical presentation; adjusting for it would block part of the effect being attributed. Mediator, not confounder.

per_column.name: multisystem_involvement
per_column.rationale: Underlying multisystem disease is a patient/clinical characteristic that raises the need for workup/intervention AND lengthens the visit; a plausible common cause surfaced from data.

per_column.name: vital_sign_abnormality_present
per_column.rationale: Abnormal vitals reflect patient severity, plausibly driving both intervention decisions and visit length; a pre-treatment severity indicator acting as a common cause.

per_column.name: procedure_or_intervention_performed
per_column.rationale: This is a candidate cause whose effect on duration is being attributed -- performing an in-office/invasive procedure directly consumes visit time. Serves as the treatment.

per_column.name: medication_initiation_or_adjustment
per_column.rationale: Another candidate clinical action whose effect on duration is under attribution; starting/adjusting medication adds counseling and documentation time.

per_column.name: patient_age_group
per_column.rationale: Age influences disease complexity and the treatments pursued as well as visit pacing/duration; a classic common cause. Note it duplicates the existing age_group column, but semantically a confounder.

per_column.name: visit_type
per_column.rationale: Whether a visit is a new problem, follow-up, or preventive shapes both what interventions occur and how long the encounter runs; a structural pre-encounter common cause.

judge.rationale: The added columns do set up a causal estimation: they supply candidate treatments (procedure/intervention performed, medication initiation/adjustment) whose effect on visit_duration is being attributed, and several genuine confounders that are pre-treatment common causes of both the clinical actions taken and the visit length -- primary_complaint_type, multisystem_involvement, vital_sign_abnormality_present, and visit_type. None of these were named in the query (which only says 'clinical factors'), so they demonstrate real surfacing of confounders from the domain. Weaknesses: diagnostic_workup_required is a mediator on the treatment->outcome path and should not be adjusted for; patient_age_group merely duplicates the existing age_group; and the operator does not cleanly separate a single treatment from confounders, mixing multiple candidate causes. Overall a partially successful realisation of causal attribution with meaningful non-query confounders but a mediator contamination that lowers quality.
